subject: Agriculture
title: Why Soil Color Matters
description: Learn Why Soil Color Matters in one minute.

hook.text: Dark soil, red soil, gray soil, white soil—each color tells you something about what's inside.

buildup.text: Dark brown or black soil is rich in organic matter. That darkness means fertility.

discovery.text: Red and orange soils contain iron oxides. They're common in tropical regions with heavy weathering.

twist.text: Gray or blue-gray soil signals waterlogging. Lack of oxygen changes iron chemistry and drains the color.

climax.text: Soil scientists use a Munsell color chart—the same tool used for paint—to classify soil precisely.

punchline.text: Read the color, read the soil. Nature labels everything.

quiz.question: What does dark brown or black soil typically indicate?
options: High organic matter content and fertility
